name: stage-soft-edge-blur
summary: a generic stage of mocha-stage: the alpha channel, or all four channels, of each frame blurred with a box blur, a repeated box blur or a Gaussian blur of the soft-edge crate; a published method under explicit configuration, not compared with any product

binaries.name: mocha-stage
binaries.arguments: apply soft-edge-blur --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --fps N[/D] [--frames N] [--describe] [--param K=V]... [--layer keys=PATH]
binaries.stdin: whole raw frames; not read with --describe
binaries.stdout: the frames of the stage, nothing else; with --describe one line of JSON
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

frame_contract: frames/2 raw frames: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, straight alpha, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame

parameters.maps_to: Which channels are blurred: the alpha channel, or all four; the others pass.
The blur: one box blur, passes box blurs in a row, or a Gaussian blur.
The box radius in samples, or the Gaussian sigma or radius as gauss_spec says; 0 is no blur; may be keyed.
The number of box blurs in a row; read when method is box-repeated.
Whether radius is the standard deviation of the Gaussian or a radius divided by radius_to_sigma (GaussSpec); read when method is gaussian.
What a tap outside the frame reads (Config::border).
How a box radius with a fraction becomes weights (Config::frac_rule).
The Gaussian is cut at this many standard deviations (Config::trunc_k); the Gaussian needs a value above 0.
How the Gaussian weights are evaluated (Config::exp_method).
The number of terms of the exponential series (Config::exp_terms).
A Gaussian given by radius has sigma = radius / this value (Config::radius_to_sigma); it needs a value above 0.

layers.meaning: A key file with a value per frame for radius.

geometry: preserve: the output has the width, height, depth, rate and frame count of the input; --describe answers the geometry of the request and refuses values the crate refuses
sample_rule: computed on f32 samples: an integer sample v is v / 255 or v / 65535, computed in f64 and rounded once to f32; on the way out a sample x is floor(clamp(x, 0, 1) * max + 0.5) and a sample that is not a number is 0; depth 32 samples are the stream's own floats and are never clamped; each chosen channel is blurred as a one channel buffer with box_blur, box_blur_repeated or gaussian_blur; the other channels pass
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, one line on standard error, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame, broken_pipe or stage_failed

exit_codes_table.means: every input frame was processed and written, or --describe printed its answer
stage_failed: the output could not be written for a reason other than a closed pipe
usage: a bad or missing option, a parameter or a layer given twice, a layer with an empty path
unsupported: a depth the stage does not take, a parameter or a layer the stage does not have, a value the stage refuses
bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe: a failed read, input that ends inside a frame, a frame count other than --frames, a layer file that cannot be read or parsed, a reader that went away
exit_codes_table.table: the table's bad_input, partial_frame and broken_pipe

unpinned_paths.why: a write to standard output that fails for a reason other than a closed pipe; no test makes one, because it needs a device that differs between systems
a reader that closes the pipe while the stage writes; the convention's conformance tool exercises it, the rows of this file do not
